messages.author: 6470a286784cd889
messages.subject: Problem with model identification
parts:
Dear all, I am a beginner in R and Lavaan and I have a basic question


I decided to give it a try with Lavaan, especially to use its robust methods.


I got stuck trying to fit a model for a CFA of an already published scale (we are trying to show evidence of validity of it). I managed to replicate AMOS’s results (using ML estimator) for the first order measures, but this one involves second order factors and I can’t set the model right.


I have managed to run the analysis, but I keep getting a different df from the original measure (they had 71 and I got 73), which makes me believe I have done something wrong, probably when I tried to fixed some of the second order factor parameters.


Here is what I have done:


Model <-

 'F1 =~ F1_1 + F1_2 + F1_3;

F2 =~ F2_1 + F2_2 + F2_3 +  F2_4;           

F3 =~ F3_1 + F3_2 + F3_3;

F4 =~ F4_1 + F4_2;

F5 =~ F5_1 + F5_2;

FF1 =~ 1*F1 + F2 + F3;

FF2 =~ 1*F4 + F5;

FF1 ~~ FF2'

Model.fit <- cfa(Model, data = CFA, estimator = "MLM", std.lv = FALSE)


Could anyone please tell me how should I do it correctly? Sorry for such a basic question, but I couldn't figure it out by myself.


I tried to fix also one parameter in each first order factor:


Model <-

 'F1 =~ 1*F1_1 + F1_2 + F1_3;

F2 =~ 1*F2_1 + F2_2 + F2_3 +  F2_4;           

F3 =~ 1*F3_1 + F3_2 + F3_3;

F4 =~ 1*F4_1 + F4_2;

F5 =~ 1*F5_1 + F5_2;

FF1 =~ 1*F1 + F2 + F3;

FF2 =~ 1*F4 + F5;

FF1 ~~ FF2'


But then I got the message:


Warning messages:
1: In lav_object_post_check(lavobject) :
  lavaan WARNING: some estimated variances are negative
2: In lav_object_post_check(lavobject) :
  lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite; use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate.


Thank you very much for any help!


Best,


Tiago

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Problem with model identification
parts:
If you are setting std.lv = FALSE, then fixing the first loadings to 1 in the syntax is redundant (read the ?lavaan help page and the tutorial pages: http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cfa.html).  Not knowing anything about the model fit in Amos, I can't say why your df differ, but your model is identified.  And the model runs without error -- just a warning about a Heywood case.  You can search for information about that on Google or an introductory text on SEM / CFA.

Terry

messages.author: 6470a286784cd889
messages.subject: Re: Problem with model identification
parts:
Dear Terrence, thank you very much for such promptly reply.

Indeed, the model runs fine, and the second alternative does has the same df, as it should be. Because of the warning message I thought that it wouldn't run, it was a dumb supposition of mine.
I'll see what I can do concerning the Heywood case.

Thanks again!

Tiago
